payload.title: Testing a claim about the proportion of district students that ride the bus to school

stimulus.description: A district report states that $50\%$ of its students ride the bus to school. A parent group suspects that the true proportion is higher. A random sample of $200$ students is selected, and $116$ of them ride the bus to school. Use a significance level of $\alpha=0.05$.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: State the null and alternative hypotheses for the test described. Define any parameter you use.
parts.model_answer: Let $p$ be the proportion of all district students that ride the bus to school. $H_0: p = 0.5$ and $H_a: p > 0.5$.

rubric_rows.criterion: States the null hypothesis $H_0: p = 0.5$ with $p$ defined as the population proportion in context
common_errors: writes hypotheses about the sample proportion

rubric_rows.criterion: States the alternative hypothesis $H_a: p > 0.5$ in the direction of the suspicion

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Verify that the conditions for a one-sample z-test for a proportion are met. There are about $20000$ students in all.
parts.model_answer: Random: the sample is random. 10% condition: $200$ is less than 10% of $20000$. Large counts: $np_0 = 100 \ge 10$ and $n(1-p_0) = 100 \ge 10$.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the sample is random and that the sample size 200 is less than 10% of the population (20000)
common_errors: checks the conditions with the sample proportion instead of the sample size

rubric_rows.criterion: Checks the large counts condition with the null value: $np_0 = 100$ and $n(1-p_0) = 100$ are both at least $10$
common_errors: uses the sample proportion for the large counts check

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Carry out the test: identify the procedure, and calculate the test statistic and the P-value.
parts.model_answer: One-sample z-test for a proportion. $\hat p = 116/200 = 0.5800$, $z = (0.5800 - 0.5)/\sqrt{0.5(0.5)/200} \approx 2.26$, P-value $\approx 0.0118$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Names the procedure: a one-sample z-test for a population proportion
Calculates the test statistic (answer z of about 2.26)
common_errors: uses the sample proportion in the standard error

rubric_rows.criterion: Finds the P-value from the standard normal distribution for the one-sided alternative (answer about 0.0118)
common_errors: doubles the P-value for a one-sided test

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: State a conclusion in the context of the problem. Justify your answer using the P-value and the significance level.
parts.model_answer: The P-value $0.0118$ is less than $0.05$, so reject $H_0$. There is convincing evidence that the proportion of all district students that ride the bus to school is higher than 0.5.

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares the P-value (0.0118) with the significance level 0.05 (less)
common_errors: compares the test statistic with alpha

rubric_rows.criterion: Makes the decision: rejects the null hypothesis
States the conclusion about the population in context (convincing evidence)
required_elements: conclusion in context about the population

payload.title: Planning a study of adult members of a community center

stimulus.description: Five-number summary of the self-rated stress score for a sample of adult members of a community center.

data.notes: Summary of the self-rated stress score for a sample of adult members of a community center.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: A researcher plans a study of adult members of a community center. For each person the researcher records whether a member takes a weekly yoga class and the self-rated stress score. Identify the explanatory variable and the response variable in this study.
parts.model_answer: Explanatory variable: whether a member takes a weekly yoga class. Response variable: the self-rated stress score.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the explanatory variable as whether a member takes a weekly yoga class
required_elements: whether a member takes a weekly yoga class

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the response variable as the self-rated stress score
common_errors: names the group as the response

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: The table shown gives the five-number summary of the self-rated stress score for the sample. (i) Calculate the interquartile range. (ii) Is a value of $90$ points an outlier according to the $1.5\times\mathrm{IQR}$ rule? Justify your answer with a calculation.
parts.model_answer: (i) IQR = 73 - 60 = 13. (ii) The upper boundary is 73 + 1.5(13) = 92.5; since 90 is not greater than 92.5, 90 is not an outlier.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the interquartile range (answer 13)
common_errors: uses the range instead of the IQR

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares 90 with the boundary Q3 + 1.5 IQR = 92.5 and states that it is not an outlier

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The researcher is considering an experiment with $40$ volunteers from all adult members of the center. (i) Describe a method to assign each volunteer at random to one of the two groups so that the groups are the same size. (ii) Explain why random assignment makes it reasonable to conclude that a difference in the self-rated stress score was caused by the treatment.
parts.model_answer: (i) Number the volunteers, use a random number generator (or draw names from a hat) to choose half of them for the treatment group; the rest form the other group. (ii) Random assignment tends to balance other variables across the groups, so a difference in the response is attributable to the treatment.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes a chance method (random numbers, names from a hat) that puts half of the volunteers in each group
alt_solutions: shuffle names and take the first half

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains that random assignment balances other (lurking) variables between the groups so cause and effect can be concluded
common_errors: says random assignment makes the sample representative of the population

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Suppose that instead the researcher simply compares adult members of a community center who already chose to take a yoga class with those who chose to not take a yoga class. Can the researcher conclude that whether a member takes a weekly yoga class causes a change in the self-rated stress score? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: No. This is an observational study; the groups chose themselves, so other variables (confounders) may explain the difference and a cause-and-effect conclusion is not justified.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that a cause-and-effect conclusion is not justified because the individuals chose their own groups (observational study, confounding possible)
common_errors: claims the difference proves cause because the result is significant

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: The researcher also wants to study the number of hours per week that members use the center among all adult members of the center. State a valid investigative question about this topic that requires a statistical investigation. Your question should name the population of interest, name the variable that would be measured, and be answerable by collecting and analyzing data that vary from individual to individual.
parts.model_answer: For example: What is the typical number of hours per week that adult members of the center use the center?

rubric_rows.criterion: Names the population of interest (all adult members of the center)
required_elements: all adult members of the center
common_errors: names only the sample or one individual

rubric_rows.criterion: Names the variable that would be measured (the number of hours per week that members use the center)
required_elements: the number of hours per week that members use the center

rubric_rows.criterion: Poses a question that anticipates variability among individuals and can be answered with data (not a single fact or an opinion)
